CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is the City of Salatiga.
7. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
9. Gender-Based Violence is any act based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life, including domestic violence.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Salatiga.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit within the Regional Government that carries out certain regional government affairs based on the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of Victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Implementation of Protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of Violence, case handling and post-crisis handling, coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation.
10. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb as referred to in Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
11. Violence against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion, and all forms of treatment carried out against children that results in and is not limited to physical, sexual, psychological violence, economic exploitation, including neglect and ill-treatment that degrades the dignity of the Child.
12. Complaint is notification regarding an incident of violence either in writing or orally by the Victim or other parties to interested parties.
13. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
14. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, as well as interpreters for the purpose of self-strengthening of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children to resolve the problems faced.
15. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and Victims that supports the reunification of Victims into the family environment or family substitute that can provide Protection and fulfillment of the Victim's needs.
16. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide Protection to Victims.

Article 14
(1) Coordination and cooperation as referred to in Article 10 letter d, includes:
a. conducting coordination and cooperation between regions in handling cases of Gender-Based Violence and Children;

(2) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes Assistance, referral, repatriation, Social Reintegration, and development of integrated Service systems.
2.1.rationale: The policy explicitly provides for coordination and cooperation across regions (jurisdictions) in handling cases, indicating an institutional network beyond a single locality.

2.2.evidence:
CHAPTER V
ORGANIZATION
Article 17
(1) The Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children shall be carried out by a non-structural institution under the coordination of the SKPD responsible for women's empowerment and Child Protection.
(2) The non-structural institution as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of elements of the Regional Government, elements of vertical agencies in the field of law enforcement, elements of the community, and elements of related stakeholders.
(3) The non-structural institution as referred to in paragraph (1) shall have the duties to:
a. implement Protection efforts for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children, covering prevention, case handling, post-crisis handling, as well as monitoring and reporting;
b. formulate action plans, programs, and activities for the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children;
c. formulate service standards for the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children; and
d. report the results of task implementation and be accountable to the Mayor.
(4) Further provisions regarding the establishment, membership, and description of duties as well as working procedures of the non-structural institution as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.
2.2.rationale: The policy establishes a non-structural institution composed not only of government and law enforcement elements but also community and related stakeholders, which constitutes a formal collaboration mechanism with non-government actors/service providers.

2.3.rationale: While the policy mentions monitoring, documentation, and reporting, none of the provided passages explicitly establish a data collection or information system for VAW/women’s protection (e.g., a dedicated database/system, procedures, or institutionalized information system).

2.4.rationale: The passages reference gender equality/justice principles and a non-structural institution for victim protection, but they do not specifically mention gender mainstreaming institutionalisation or a dedicated gender mainstreaming working group to deliver VAW policies and programs.

2.5.rationale: The policy assigns the regional government responsibility to enhance the capacity of service provider institutions, which constitutes an explicit commitment to capacity building for those delivering services.

2.6.evidence:
CHAPTER VIII
GUIDANCE, CONTROL, AND SUPERVISION
Article 23
Guidance and control of the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children includes:
a. provision of guidelines, instructions, guidance and direction, as well as supervision;
b. coordination of the preparation and implementation of action plans, programs, and activities;
c. provision of consultation on the implementation of programs and activities as well as provision of solutions to obstacles encountered; and
d. implementation of monitoring and evaluation.
2.6.rationale: The policy explicitly includes implementation of monitoring and evaluation as part of guidance and control of policy implementation.

3.4.rationale: The policy explicitly provides for temporary protection in safe houses (shelters) as part of case handling.

3.5.rationale: The policy includes conducting legal assistance in handling and resolving cases, indicating provision of legal assistance services for victims.

3.6.rationale: The policy provides for physical recovery at health service institutions as part of post-crisis handling, indicating access to health/medical services.

3.7.rationale: The policy includes psychosocial recovery and assistance in post-crisis handling, which constitutes psychosocial counselling/support services.

3.8.rationale: The policy includes spiritual guidance services as part of post-crisis handling, indicating religious/spiritual counselling support.

3.9.rationale: The policy assigns the regional government responsibility to provide recovery and social reintegration services, which corresponds to resocialisation/rehabilitation and reintegration support.

3.10.rationale: The policy includes skills training services and increasing economic access as part of post-crisis handling, indicating economic empowerment/support services.

5.7.rationale: The policy explicitly assigns obligations and responsibilities to the community, family, and parents to prevent violence, report incidents, and participate in handling victims, indicating direct engagement with the community.

6.1.rationale: The passages describe general protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, including prevention and mapping violence-prone areas, but do not mention conflict zones, disaster-prone areas, or special measures for women in such contexts.

6.2.rationale: The cited provisions cover victims of gender-based violence and children generally, without any explicit or implicit reference to human trafficking or tailored protections for trafficking victims.

6.3.rationale: None of the passages mention women workers/employees or workplace-specific protections; they focus on general victim protection for gender-based violence and children.

6.4.rationale: The passages do not reference elderly women or age-specific protections; they provide general victim rights and services.

Article 2
letter a What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of Gender-Based and Child Violence without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status, and physical and mental condition.
letter b What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, must be the primary consideration.
letter c What is meant by "Gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

letter l What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure Victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of Victims.
letter m What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the victim's right to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.

6.8.rationale: While victims are referenced as potential witnesses and entitled to protection, the passages do not specifically address women in conflict with the law as witnesses or perpetrators, nor provide women-specific legal-process protections.

6.9.rationale: Although non-discrimination mentions ethnicity and culture, there is no explicit mention of Indigenous peoples/masyarakat adat or any special measures targeted to them.

6.10.rationale: The passages include repatriation assistance and social reintegration for victims generally, but do not mention refugees, forced displacement, or targeted protections for displaced populations.

6.11.rationale: There is no mention of domestic workers as a group or any specific protections tailored to domestic work contexts; the text addresses gender-based violence and child victims generally.

6.12.rationale: The policy provides temporary protection in shelters/safe houses for victims, but does not address homelessness or women experiencing homelessness as a targeted group.

6.13.rationale: None of the passages mention former inmates/correctional institutions or provide protections targeted at formerly incarcerated women; the focus remains on victims of gender-based violence and children.
